correctness.rationale: The six-state two-phase Markov kernel is obtained from the explicit fitness-weighted parent/neighbor update, with two absorbing states and strictly transient four-state complement for all r>0. An exact four-by-four Cramer determinant representation expands to two polynomial identities, verified coefficient-by-coefficient by the dependency-free included verifier. Both difference signs follow from r-1 and strictly positive polynomial factors; independent unreduced eight-state rational checks agree in 40 samples. Finite checking is supplemental to exact polynomial identity, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The smallest nontrivial population already changes from strict selection suppression to strict amplification when the holding time increases by one reproduction update. This closes the natural integer gap between previously reported dwell-one suppression and dwell-ten amplification, with global fitness-uniform inequalities rather than a numerical sampling grid. Comparison to previously analyzed two-path switches shows the second contact topology materially changes the first possible amplification horizon. The result is a mathematically motivated finite-size threshold, not an arbitrary enumeration.
